analysis.title: Weekly Economic Roundup, 16 November 2026
key_insights: PNC calls recent data decidedly hawkish. Last week's inflation readings were hot and broad-based, and October job growth was more than double consensus. The report says this means employment is no longer the Fed's primary concern.
PNC says a 25bp Fed hike at the December FOMC is a lock ("all but a certainty"). Its stated reason is that inflation is too high and broader than the knock-on effects of higher energy prices.

Markets price roughly a 10% chance of a 50bp hike in December. The main reason is a speech by Fed Governor Chris Waller before the CPI release. He said he would back 25bp even if inflation moderated, but that core CPI of 0.3% or higher could warrant a larger hike. October core CPI came in at 0.3%.

PNC does not expect 50bp in December but says the risk has shifted toward a faster pace of tightening. Its baseline is a hike at every other meeting. Consecutive 25bp hikes are the alternative if inflation stays stubbornly high.
October nonfarm payrolls rose a net 165k, with large upward revisions to prior months. The unemployment rate fell slightly on the month and is down 40bps from last year's high.

October core CPI was 0.3%, above expectations for the third straight month. The Producer Price Index for intermediate goods and services has accelerated to 8% year-over-year, second only to the 2022 inflation spike.

PNC expects a tepid October retail sales report on Tuesday 11/17: 0.3% m/m headline, with retail sales ex autos at 0.4%. September and August were boosted by gasoline station sales, which rose 6.4% in September and 4.0% in August on higher fuel prices.

PNC attributes the expected October slowdown in retail sales to slower wage growth, lower seasonally adjusted gas prices, a drop in auto sales and low household savings. It says persistent inflation is weighing on household purchasing power, although the longer-term spending trend remains healthy.

The calendar this week includes industrial production, housing starts, the FOMC minutes (Wed 11/18, 2:00 pm), the Philadelphia Fed survey, jobless claims, the Leading Index and final University of Michigan sentiment. PNC forecasts a slower rise in industrial production after a utilities-driven jump in September, a modest recovery in housing starts and a better sentiment reading on falling gas prices.

tension_points.bull_case: Faster tightening case: core CPI at 0.3% for October met Waller's stated threshold for a possible larger hike. Markets already price about a 10% chance of 50bp.
tension_points.bear_case: PNC's base case is that the Fed hikes 25bp in December, with a hike at every other meeting. Waller said exact timing matters less than ensuring the expected tightening occurs, so a larger single move is not needed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Waller said core CPI of 0.3% or higher could warrant a larger hike. The report does not name a level that would rule out a 50bp hike.
